content.user_title: Build Consistent Apps Across Every Platform
content.value_statement: Cross-platform teams often ship inconsistent features and repeat architecture decisions. This skill structures API design, implementation, testing, and optimization across web, iOS, Android, and desktop.
actual_capabilities: Defines REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket contracts before platform implementation.
Plans shared data models, business rules, state management, caching, and error handling.
Coordinates parallel implementations for React, SwiftUI, Kotlin Compose, and Electron or Tauri.
Creates platform-aware design guidance covering accessibility, themes, responsive layouts, and native conventions.
Builds feature parity matrices with functional, performance, accessibility, and resilience checks.
Documents platform optimizations, deployment requirements, and architecture trade-offs.
limitations: Requires a clear feature specification and target platform list.
Provides workflow guidance but does not replace platform-specific build tools or developer accounts.
Generated implementations still require testing on real browsers, devices, and operating systems.
Referenced specialized subagents may not exist in every supported tool.

use_cases.title: Launch a feature on four platforms
use_cases.description: Plan one API contract and coordinate consistent web, iOS, Android, and desktop implementations.

use_cases.title: Standardize platform architecture
use_cases.description: Define shared models, business rules, state patterns, and adapters while preserving native user experiences.

use_cases.title: Verify feature parity
use_cases.description: Create a testing matrix that compares behavior, accessibility, performance, and network resilience across platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Outline a cross-platform feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan [feature] for [platforms]. Identify requirements, shared behavior, platform differences, dependencies, and measurable success criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a defined feature.

prompt_templates.title: Design the shared API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an API-first architecture for [feature]. Include endpoints, models, authentication, validation, errors, caching, offline behavior, and platform integration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate parallel implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create parallel workstreams for [platforms] using [API contract]. Define shared milestones, platform tasks, synchronization points, tests, and acceptance criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced delivery planning for several teams.

prompt_templates.title: Audit parity and readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these platform implementations: [details]. Produce a parity matrix, identify gaps, assess performance and accessibility, and prioritize release blockers.

output_examples.input: Plan account recovery for web, iOS, and Android.
output_examples.output: A phased plan covering recovery APIs, shared states, native screens, security checks, parallel workstreams, and platform acceptance tests.

output_examples.input: Compare offline synchronization across our mobile applications.
output: Shared conflict resolution rules and retry policies.
Platform storage and background execution differences.
A parity matrix with failure scenarios and expected outcomes.

output_examples.input: Prepare a desktop release readiness review.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review of signing, installers, updates, operating system integration, resource usage, testing coverage, and unresolved release risks.

best_practices: Finalize shared contracts and acceptance criteria before platform teams begin implementation.
Preserve native interaction patterns while keeping behavior and data rules consistent.
Test real devices and operating systems at regular synchronization points.
anti_patterns: Do not copy one platform interface directly onto every other platform.
Do not begin parallel implementation with unresolved API or data model decisions.
Do not declare parity from screenshots without testing behavior, accessibility, performance, and failure states.

faq.question: Which platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers web, iOS, Android, and optional desktop applications built with Electron or Tauri.

faq.question: Does it require one shared codebase?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates shared logic where useful while supporting native implementations and platform-specific adapters.

faq.question: Can it generate an API specification?
faq.answer: It guides creation of REST, GraphQL, or WebSocket contracts with models, authentication, validation, errors, caching, and limits.

faq.question: Does it implement the applications automatically?
faq.answer: It coordinates implementation prompts and expected outputs. Available tools, subagents, repositories, and build environments determine execution.

faq.question: How does it assess feature parity?
faq.answer: It compares functionality, design compliance, performance, accessibility, synchronization, resilience, and complete user journeys.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the feature specification, target platforms, technical constraints, existing API details, design standards, timelines, and measurable success criteria.
